learn.objective: Read and produce clear electrical single-line diagrams (SLDs) while maintaining traceability between equipment, protection, conductors and downstream loads.
concepts: Purpose and information hierarchy of an SLD
Cable/conductor identification and basic schedule interfaces
Revision control and coordination with layouts, schedules and specifications
learn.seniorReasoning: A senior designer treats an SLD as a controlled representation of the electrical system, not merely a collection of symbols. Every major element should have a reason, an identifiable relationship to other documents, and enough information for review and coordination.

apply.scenario: Develop a fictional SLD for a small pump-station distribution system supplied from a main LV switchboard through a motor control section to two pumps and auxiliary loads.
tasks: Establish the source-to-load hierarchy and identify the major equipment tags.
Represent incomer, protective devices, feeders, motor starters/VSD interfaces and outgoing loads using a consistent symbol and annotation strategy.
Create a simple cable/feeder identification scheme and identify which information should come from a cable schedule rather than being duplicated on the SLD.
Cross-check the SLD against a fictional equipment list and identify at least three discrepancies or missing inputs.
Prepare a short issue-readiness checklist covering consistency, references, tags, revisions and coordination interfaces.
apply.deliverable: A sanitized SLD exercise plus a discrepancy/assumption register and issue-readiness checklist.

questions.prompt: An equipment tag appears on the SLD but not in the equipment list. What is the strongest senior response?
questions.answer: Treat it as a coordination discrepancy, trace the source of the tag and confirm the intended equipment before issuing the drawing rather than silently creating or deleting information.

questions.prompt: Why should a cable schedule not simply be copied in full onto every SLD?
questions.answer: The SLD should communicate system relationships and key design information while detailed cable data remains controlled in its schedule; unnecessary duplication increases inconsistency risk.

questions.prompt: A protective device rating changes on the design input. What should be checked beyond changing the number on the SLD?
questions.answer: Check affected feeder/cable information, equipment interfaces, schedules, downstream loads, coordination assumptions and revision impacts before issue.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a senior SLD review from a symbol-by-symbol visual check?
questions.answer: It verifies system logic, source-to-load traceability, interfaces, identifiers, design inputs, document consistency and issue readiness.

evidence.prompt: Capture a sanitized SLD exercise and supporting discrepancy/QA record demonstrating that you can communicate system relationships and identify coordination issues before issue.
criteria: Equipment and feeder identifiers are traceable

integration.home: Use this module as a next-best-action when the learner reaches Week 4.
integration.journal: Prompt reflection on system traceability, discrepancies found and decisions escalated.
integration.portfolio: Store the sanitized SLD plus discrepancy/QA record as evidence of system-documentation capability.
